title: Dark Soul
snippet: Using the Dark Soul, the Pygmy created black sprites of darkness called Humanity, which was given to his descendants. These dark-souled beings risen from the Abyss were called Humans, and each bore a small fragment of the Dark Soul. When the other Lords began fighting against the Everlasting Dragons, they conscripted the Humans into the forces, who aided the Lords by forging quasi-living arms and armor deep within the Abyss. But the Humans were betrayed by the Lords, for they feared the Dark that resides within each and every one of them. Their contributions to the War of the Ancients went completely unrecorded, and upon their Humanity, the Gods placed a sealing ring of fire, later to be known as the Darksign.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : Although he was killed, the Dark Soul of Manus was so large and powerful that he was reborn in death, and his soul split into miniscule fragments that retained some will. These pieces began to coalesce once again by absorbing other humanities, becoming the incarnations of different emotions of Manus and then human in shape, with their own self-awareness: Elana was the embodiment of Manus' wrath, Alsanna of his fear, Nadalia of his solitude and Nashandra, the tiniest fragment of Manus, the embodiment of his want. These new entities had some recollection of their father and his dark powers and when the Abyss that they called home was dissipated they scattered across the land. To sustain themselves and seek power, they reached Drangleic where in one way or another they came into contact with the holders of magnificent souls, drawn to their awesome strength.

title: Dark Soul
snippet:
Dark Soul -  Dark Souls - item - capabilities 
 capabilities : Any fragment of the Dark Soul that separates from the original can be fueled by emotions and willpower, and increase its usable power, making it the most unique of the four Lord Souls.

Most notable of its functions is the power to animate life and raise sentient beings from the Abyss, for the Dark Soul is the only Lord Soul which is intrinsically tied to the Abyss, unlike the other forms of life that take energy from Souls. The main lifeform connected to it is the Human race, but lesser creatures are said to have also risen from the Dark, such as the White-faced Locust. The Dark Soul is also linked to the Dark Hand, and by extension, the art of Lifedrain. This is the legendary power of the fabled Dark Lord, used to gain humanity from others. The Darkwraiths used this power to steal Humanity from their victims.

title: Abyss
snippet:
Abyss -  Dark Souls - location - lead 
 lead : The **Abyss** is a location in *Dark Souls*, as well as a storyline concept featured in all three games in the series.

The in-game location is at the heart of the New Londo Ruins, a featureless expanse where the Chosen Undead must slay the Four Kings and can encounter Darkstalker Kaathe. As a concept, "Abyss" is the name given to both a force that consumes or corrupts most forms of life, and to the areas in which it dwells; it is tied to the Age of Dark, and also gave birth to a twisted offshoot known as The Deep.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: What exactly the term "Age of Dark" implies is never made explicitly clear in the games, however it is stated in the canonical *Dark Souls Trilogy Compendium* to be a time when the Light fades, a Dark Lord is heralded, and humanity dominates the world. When the protagonists are given information about the Age of Dark, it typically comes from the mouths of potentially unreliable narrators, of whom Kaathe and his counterpart, Kingseeker Frampt, are examples. Kaathe asserts that the Age of Dark is "the age of men," presumably meaning the Age of those possessing Humanity in contrast to the Age of the Gods, and also declares that Gwyn "resisted the course of nature" when he linked the Flame and prolonged the Age of Fire.

title: Age of Dark
snippet:
Age of Dark -  Dark Souls - storyline - lore 
 lore : The Age of Dark begins when the First Flame fades completely, thus ending the Age of Fire and the rule of the gods that gained their power from it.
Since the Flame continues to burn until it goes out naturally, the Dark Age should have arrived, as naturally, when it had exhausted its fuel.

Despite the Age of Dark being a ubiquitous concept throughout the *Dark Souls* series, it is never the "current" state of the world in any of the existing games. Each of the *Dark Souls* games takes place during a late point in the Age of Fire, a point which could theoretically lead to the beginning of the Age of Dark, but which does not do so during the normal course of gameplay, with one possible exception.

title: Dark Hand
snippet:
Dark Hand -  Dark Souls - weapon - general_information 
 general_information : As a shield, the Dark Hand has an 80% damage reduction from all damage types, is able to parry, is tied with the Small Leather Shield for lowest weight in the game, and one of the highest lightning damage reductions of all shields. This makes the Dark Hand a very well rounded Small Shield alternative. It also has the highest durability available and is hidden when not actively blocking, helping to offset its very low stability negative.

As a weapon, the Dark Hand's special right handed strong attack is the only action capable of stealing liquid humanity from NPCs and other players. How much it steals is dependent on the rank the player has progressed in the Darkwraith Covenant, as listed:
+0 (or not in the Darkwraith covenant): 1 humanity stolen
+1: 3 humanity stolen
+2: 5 humanity stolen
+3: 10 humanity stolen

title: Furtive Pygmy
snippet:
Furtive Pygmy -  Dark Souls - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : The Furtive Pygmy is one of the primordial humanoids that appeared underground following the advent of the First Flame which brought "disparity"—heat and cold, life and death, light and dark. He was the one who found the Dark Soul among the four Lord Souls, the other three of which were discovered by Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight, Gravelord Nito, and the Witch of Izalith.

The Furtive Pygmy fragmented his Dark Soul among his descendants, creating the first Humans in the form of the Pygmies. The pygmies harnessed their peculiar Lord Soul and unlocked the life-generating capabilities of its Abyss, forging weapons and armor that adopted the properties of darkness.

title: Dark Souls II
snippet:
Dark Souls II -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - plot 
 plot : The story of *Dark Souls II* is not directly connected to *Dark Souls*, though they are set in the same world.

The game takes place in Drangleic, a once prosperous land under the rule of King Vendrick, which has fallen to ruin throughout the ages with the raging war between humans and giants, the sudden disappearance of the King, and the spreading of the Undead Curse. Like many others, the protagonist has come to the crumbling kingdom in search of a cure for their crippling affliction, the Curse of the Undead.

title: Humans
snippet:
Humans -  Dark Souls III - character - description 
 description : Like the Gods, the race of Men varies in size and physical appearance, but are almost consistently amongst the shortest of the races. It seems that size is naturally varied and has been for all time, as the Ringed Knights are towering figures, while the Pygmy Lords are slightly shorter than modern man.

All human beings are made Human by a fragment of the Dark Soul, known as their Humanity, which looks like a black sprite with blank white eyes. Humans are also capable of withstanding the Abyss, provided that they have not become untuned to it, and even find a sort of comfort in it.

By the time of that human's death, their Humanity could be in any number of states. Emotion seems to make Humanity stronger, but also unstable, and the human body can be mutated by its own essence if control is lost.

title: Timeline
snippet:
The Catacombs of Carthus, an immense underground necropolis, are built to keep and bury the bones of countless people and soldiers
High Lord Wolnir uses necromancy to reanimate himself and control a skeleton army and empire, wishing to remain the last being
An Abyss opens in the Catacombs of Carthus and Wolnir falls into it, experiencing the terror of true darkness and he pleads to the gods for the first time
The sword and three sacred armlets he stole give him a semblance of comfort and prevent him from being corrupted by the Abyss, which is contained in a magical artifact
After falling into the Abyss, Wolnir discovers a form of pyromancy that uses the dark souls, and since it's connected with humanity it gained a will of its own
After Wolnir's fall into the Abyss, the pyromancers become the guardians of the catacombs
After Wolnir's fall into the Abyss, the pyromancers discover the dark flame, born from the Abyss and shadowless, that spawned from the flames of humanity
